findings.claim: The 'pit' recurrence sentence names the wrong Hebrew tokens: it cites 33:18's מֵעֲבֹ֥ר and 33:22's נַפְשׁ֑וֹ as the bare and prefixed pit forms, when the pit tokens are 33:18 שָׁ֑חַת (bare) and 33:22 לַשַּׁ֣חַת (prefixed).
findings.grounds: The sweep arithmetic is exact: sweep.py --skel over the 'pit' skeleton שחת returns 7 VERSES book-wide - Job.9.31, Job.17.14, Job.33.18, Job.33.22, Job.33.24, Job.33.28, Job.33.30 - which is the row's member list verbatim. The two Hebrew tokens the sentence names, however, are not 'pit'. oshb:Job.33.18 word 6 is מֵעֲבֹ֥ר, the preposition-plus-infinitive rendered by WEB as "from perishing", and it carries a mem prefix, so it is not 'bare'; oshb:Job.33.22 word 3 is נַפְשׁ֑וֹ, "his soul", a suffixed form with no prefix, so it is not 'prefixed'. The actual 'pit' tokens are oshb:Job.33.18 word 4 שָׁ֑חַת (bare, etnachta) and oshb:Job.33.22 word 2 לַשַּׁ֣חַת (prefixed lamed with assimilated article, munach) - which is exactly the bare-versus-prefixed, not-pointed-identical contrast the sentence asserts, so the claim's substance is right and only the splices are wrong. Both mis-spliced runs are byte-valid substrings of the verses they are cited from, so the mechanical guard passes clean (normalize_hebrew_in_json.py over the shipped rows: 24 ok, 0 fixed, 0 defects): the error is semantic, the wrong-token-splice class. findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair only: replace "33:18's bare מֵעֲבֹ֥ר" with the bare pit token of oshb:Job.33.18, שָׁ֑חַת, and "33:22 carries its own prefixed form נַפְשׁ֑וֹ" with the prefixed pit token of oshb:Job.33.22, לַשַּׁ֣חַת, splicing both from verse_map_oshb.json rather than retyping.
